title: I trained a 2B vision model to guess which Steam game is more popular from one screenshot.
author: zjgkkn
selftext:
I fine-tuned Qwen3.5-2B (LoRA) on Steam store screenshots. The input is one screenshot plus the game's release year, genres and 5 user tags. The output is the number of reviews the game got, as a class.

It was tested on 2026 games it never saw. Shown a pair of games from the same genre, it picks the one with more reviews 75–78% of the time. People playing the same pairs get about 62% so far. You can try to beat it here: [https://skolko-otzyvov.pages.dev/](https://skolko-otzyvov.pages.dev/)

What I actually use it for: Claude can now get feedback on its own scenes without me. It renders in-game screenshots and asks the model for a forecast. Then it finds similar Steam screenshots that did well, using Shot Search (DINOv2 for layout and lighting, SigLIP for what's in the frame), and reworks the scene. The image shows how one scene changed over those rounds.

\- Model: [https://huggingface.co/zjgkkn/qwen3.5-2b-steam-reviews-lora](https://huggingface.co/zjgkkn/qwen3.5-2b-steam-reviews-lora)

\- Training code: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/qwen\_review](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/qwen_review)

\- Reference search (index + MCP server): [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/games/shotsearch](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/games/shotsearch)
